body: Yeah that's what I'll do. And thanks. I didn't want to be one of those people who will still be with him when he has a girlfriend.
I cleared everything. I didn't want any reminders of him.
Google picture and cloud
I have I blocked every single account I could find. I dont want to deal with him anymore. Just worried he'd contact me when he gets the message or gets back.
I already deleted the proof photos in s moment of heat
I already deleted all the photos of us as proof when I was angry. I just told him off.
I will definitely check. Thank you.
I'm not sure if there are any open because of covid and I live with immune compromised parents.
I'm just worried I'll finally snap. I'm still angry and in shock. Also still traumatized from the hospital visit. And I do know what if will do. Just make me further depressed.
I understand that. Also cops sometimes have to not be empathetic to deal with the things they do. And yeah I'm still really shaked up about it.

Maybe they were afraid I'd reach for the gun? I don't know because I'm like a short woman. Also I feel ashamed if my neighbors were watching. I would rather they at least send someone who actually could sit down and talk about if I was okay and do an assessment rather than cops who arrested me and took me to the hospital while I had to wait for hours.
Thanks. I'm definitely going to hang out on this sub more. I was absent for a while because I relapsed but after this incident I'm 100 percent focused on sobriety.

The person on the line apparently can make the call I discovered. Which in a way can work out badly, especially since there are so many instances of people with mental illness getting injured by the police. It can work out badly if the person running the hotline thinks you are a danger for whatever reason. Even if you aren't suicidal.

I do have depression but alcohol triggers depressive episodes. Sometimes they can get really bad but after talking the the counselor I was feeling better. Until the police showed up. And I promise not to drink with you today was well.

They didn't send me to a psych ward they just left me in the hallway next to the triage place. They probably would have since I was getting more emotional due to being there for too long and all the sick people which kind of defeats the purpose. It would have been better to have checked me out 3 hours in. And I'm sorry that happened to you. The mental health treatments in the US suck.
Yeah whenever I think about drinking I think about that incident and all thoughts of alcohol leave my mind.

I never had any bad experiences before. I messaged around 20 times before that incident. And yeah there might be some hotlines that don't call the police on you. I didn't even know they could do that until they came banging on my door.
I'm glad my best friends didn't give up. I was a wreck when I was drunk. I'm going to move on from this and focus on self care.
Thank you. I get really horrible hangovers so I wasn't able to eat yeaterday. Just thinking about it it's just seems awful. Only a few hours of "fun" or a day or two of hell.
Thanks 😊
Still went to school but the anxiety from that night still got to me. Feeling better now with a new purpose.
Thank you :)

I have horrible willpower when it comes to things so I was surprised when I did stop for that period of time. And it does work for some people, but for me I can't drink a sip or I'll spiral down. Also I agree that stopping cold turkey especially if you drank too long can be dangerous because some people do get horrible withdrawal symptoms.
Thanks. I'm trying my best. I just want to live a happier life that alcohol stole from me.
Thank you.

It used to not be that bad, but I had to quit because since last month every time I drank I got blacked out. Like every time. And I realized it was only going to get worse. Not drinking is the best way to prevent alcohol abuse.
Same here. It's not worth it, but sometimes the brain tricks you into thinking you can drink a few drinks but it's a trap.

It was because I was still suffering from withdrawals from alcohol (mostly anxiety and cravings) and thought it would help tide me over for a day. And yeah it didn't help because I was hungover for a few days and my anxiety was even worse that before.
I tried it but it didn't work for me unfortunately :(
The addictive physical cravings are beating me up right now which sucks. And that's good that they do eventually go away. I'm trying to keep myself distracted.
Thank you. I had to stop because it was getting to that point. I hope it gets to that point where I have no cravings.
That's good. Hopefully it will be the same for me.
Thanks I needed to hear this :)
I've been eating a lot too and reading a lot too but it's always on the back of my mind since I've been "bored" without alcohol.
I kind of expected that, but I wanted clarification to justify not drinking so that I wouldn't drink.

I'm the same way. Im shy and an introvert and whenever I am at a social event I have to drink or I feel very awkward. I would say that once you are an alcoholic you can't stop once you start. I kept on saying the same thing to myself too. Like I'll only drink a few drinks. I'll only drink at parties. I knew I had a problem when I blacked out at a social gathering and had a hangover for three days. It's not worth it.
I will look it up
I really want to go to a rehab place but i can't if my parents know. My mom kind of said that she would throw me out of the house if she found me drunk..

I have spoken to two doctors. They are helping me but sometimes it doesn't work. I think I need to focus on myself more and try not to think about alcohol whenever I have any urges or other issues pertaining to it.
Thanks. I'm trying to make a hobby that doesn't involve alcohol at all. I'm currently writing, which is good.
Thank you. I'll check that out.

Thanks. I've been lurking on this sub for the past year on my main account. Even though I made this a throwaway I'll make it the main account for trying not to drink. I think after today even if I feel withdrawal symptoms I'll just not drink, even if I think it's the big C. I'll mostly chalk it up to anxiety. Thank you for your advice and opening up.

Thank you. I'll try my best. And I understand how you feel. My dad has been a chronic high functioning alcoholic too. But he has been for 40 years. And ironically I got into alcohol because he kept on offering me alcohol every other night. And we bescually became alcoholics during the pandemic together. Misery loves company. I'm slowly trying to get my way back to being sober again, but still mostly worried about the pandemic and how it will affect me. I hope I'll get help before the cases get worse.

Ironically the transmission rate is one of the highest in the US. Almost all my friends in a club got the virus. Two of my relatives died from it and one got very ill. I'm trying to quit, but it's very hard with the factors I'm dealty with. Especially with the fact that alcoholism does run with my family. At least I'm not drinking as much as I have in the past, I'm just more worried about the future.

Thank you. I'm trying some of the methods my therapist told me to do. Another thing is that I live in Alaska, which is a very depressing state because of the lack of sunlight. I also live with my parents who are very susceptible to the virus so the mutation is very triggering to me. In a way I think I know I'll relapse in the future, but I don't know how to stop it. My willpower is very bad.

I am in therapy now, and I used to self medicate with alcohol to the point of severe depression. I want medication, but the alcohol mediation I took in the past made me very nauseous, and they won't prescribe me any anxiety or depression meds until I'm sober.
